standard.title: Evaluate and synthesise information, ideas and perspectives
standard.description: evaluate and synthesise information, ideas and perspectives in a broad range of spoken, written and multimodal texts and respond appropriately to cultural context, purpose and audience
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can interpret information and evaluate source reliability in target language texts, responding to cultural nuance and diverse perspectives (AC9LS8C03). They have not yet evaluated and synthesised across a broad range of sources, distinguished fact from opinion systematically, or created responses that integrate multiple perspectives.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students evaluate and synthesise information, ideas and perspectives across a broad range of target language texts — distinguishing fact from opinion, comparing perspectives, and responding appropriately to cultural context, purpose and audience.

nodes.label: Distinguishing fact from opinion and evaluating perspectives
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can distinguish fact from opinion in target language texts and evaluate the perspectives presented.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two instances of fact and two of opinion in a text; evaluate the perspective of at least one text, identifying its position.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse persuasive and informative texts to recognise fact versus opinion; identify the perspective and assumptions of text producers; compare different stakeholder perspectives on an issue; evaluate texts for reliability, accuracy and bias.
wider: Compare two texts on the same topic from different stakeholder perspectives — explain what each perspective includes, excludes and assumes
Evaluate a target language community media text for perspective and bias — present findings with specific evidence
nodes.hinge_reason: Distinguishing fact from opinion and evaluating perspective is the analytical foundation for all synthesis work. Students who cannot identify the position of a text cannot synthesise across multiple perspectives.

response_modes.reason: Fact-opinion distinction and perspective evaluation requires explicit analytical frameworks. Students need to be able to articulate criteria for each before applying them spontaneously.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two instances of fact and two of opinion in a text
Identifies the perspective of at least one text and explains the assumptions it makes

nodes.label: Synthesising information across sources
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can synthesise information from multiple target language sources — grouping and presenting ideas, themes and issues in a logical and coherent manner.
nodes.minimum_width: Synthesise information from at least two sources into a coherent response that organises ideas thematically.
nodes.typical_width: Locate and research information from varied reliable sources; weigh options and organise information logically; determine what is most important or interesting from a range of sources; summarise and present synthesised information with personal perspective; create profiles of significant people or topics from multiple sources.
wider: Synthesise information from target language and English sources on the same topic — compare what each language-community source emphasises and explain what this reveals
Create a synthesis that integrates at least three different perspectives on an issue — not only summarising each but showing how they relate to each other

response_modes.reason: Synthesis requires students to move from juxtaposing sources to integrating them — identifying relationships, not only collecting information. Structured synthesis tasks scaffold this integrative thinking.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Genuine synthesis — not summarising but integrating — is the highest-order information processing task in the sequence. Width investment here builds the analytical capacity that transfers across all academic contexts.
success_criteria: Synthesises information from at least two sources into a response that organises ideas thematically
Presents a personal perspective alongside the synthesised information

nodes.label: Responding to cultural context and diverse text types
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can respond to target language texts appropriately for cultural context, purpose and audience — including expressive, creative and culturally embedded texts.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a response to at least one culturally embedded text that is appropriate to its cultural context — not only its linguistic content.
nodes.typical_width: Respond to expressive contemporary texts — songs, poems, performances, artworks; identify cultural elements that reflect target language community experience; listen to First Nations Australian stories and create profiles in the target language; express evaluative responses using expressive language; adapt texts for different contexts and audiences.
wider: Create a profile of a First Nations Australian author or storyteller in the target language — drawing on their story as source and reflecting on the cultural significance of the work
Respond to a target language community expressive text — identifying cultural elements, explaining their significance and connecting to a parallel element in Australian culture

response_modes.reason: Culturally appropriate response develops through encountering diverse text types, genres and cultural contexts. Each new cultural text type reveals different dimensions of the language-culture relationship.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Responding to First Nations Australian stories and culturally embedded expressive texts in the target language is where intercultural competence reaches its fullest expression in this sequence.
success_criteria: Produces a response to a culturally embedded text appropriate to its cultural context
Identifies at least one cultural element in the text and explains its significance

nodes.label: Adapting texts for context, purpose and audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can adapt target language texts for different contexts, purposes and audiences — making deliberate choices about language, register and content.
nodes.minimum_width: Adapt a text for a different context or audience — identifying at least two deliberate language changes made for the new context.
nodes.typical_width: Adapt formal texts for informal contexts and vice versa; change text purpose (informative to persuasive; narrative to analytical); adapt for different audience knowledge levels; create texts that respond to and incorporate information from other texts.
wider: Adapt the same content for two radically different audiences — contrast every language, register and content choice made for each
Adapt a text for a genuine external audience — reflect on whether the adaptation successfully served that audience's needs

response_modes.reason: Text adaptation integrates evaluation and synthesis (N1-N3) with production — students draw on their analysis of source texts to create purposeful adapted versions. The real audience condition is the fullest integration test.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Adapting texts for genuine external audiences is where target language production becomes genuinely purposeful mediation — not only demonstrating competence but serving a real communicative need.
success_criteria: Adapts a text for a different context or audience with at least two deliberate language changes identified
The adapted text is appropriate and coherent for the new context or audience
